votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

China will import at least 10 million metric tons of U.S. coal in 2027 and 2028. I led the push with the WH to prioritize U.S. coal exports with China. 

More coal means more jobs and more investment in Kentucky. I’ll always fight for Kentucky coal! https://t.co/xGV1bVPoXd

Thank you to @SecDuffy for bringing common sense back to America’s fuel economy standards.

Fuel efficiency naturally improves as technology advances. The Biden Administration’s fuel economy targets ignored market realities, raised costs, and created uncertainty for American manufacturers and consumers.

This week’s summit between President Trump and General Secretary Xi represents an important opportunity to hold the Chinese Communist Party accountable for providing Iran with satellite data it used to target the American military in the Middle East, buying Iranian oil and selling semiconductors used in Iranian weapons. It also represents an opportunity to reinforce deterrence in the Western Pacific by standing by the $11.1 billion in arms sales to Taiwan announced by the Trump Administration in 2025 and not backing off the additional $14 billion in arms sales to Taiwan presently under consideration.

Big Blue Nation with a Big Day! Congratulations to @CoachWillStein and the @UKFootball wildcats. https://t.co/Xc5Vgv7U1l

Iran’s terrorist activities and Putin’s war machine depend on access to money and energy revenues.

I helped lead the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctions Act through the House to tighten the screws on those financial networks and give President Trump additional leverage to confront America’s adversaries.

Peace through strength.

The @keeneland September Yearling Sale is here! 🐎

Last year was a RECORD year after we delivered 100% bonus depreciation in the Working Families Tax Cut.

Here’s to another record-breaking year for @keenelandsales and KY’s signature industry! https://t.co/3PopcfWxmk

The federal government wastes over $500 BILLION a year due to fraud.

I voted to establish a dedicated @TheJusticeDept division to root out fraud and strengthen federal, state, and local partnerships to protect YOUR tax dollars. https://t.co/KSGmWcCcd5

Thank you to Frank Jemley and the @kymanufacturing for the opportunity to talk to members during their DC fly-in week. Whether it be expansion at @Toyota and @Corning or the @Ford battery plant announcement last week, Kentucky manufacturing is on the move after the Working Families Tax Cut created the Made in America Tax Credit and 100% expensing for new facilities.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Recommit — Main Street Act (H R 6955)
roll_calls.plain_language: H.R. 6955 (Main Street Capital Access Act) lessens and otherwise modifies banking regulations, including those regarding institution formation, supervision by federal financial regulators, and bank merger requirements. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
